items.name: AI Studio
items.author: iMacroPad community
items.blurb: Keys that call AI services: an image from the text on your clipboard (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image, “Nano Banana”), a short answer to it, a video through an MCP server, and one of your own Shortcuts.
items.readme:
Keys that send the text on your clipboard to AI services and bring the answer back to your Mac.

## What you get

- **Image from clipboard**: sends your clipboard text to Gemini 2.5 Flash Image and saves the picture to Downloads/iMacroPad.
- **Answer the clipboard**: asks Gemini 2.5 Flash and puts a short answer on your clipboard.
- **Video (MCP)**: asks a video tool on an MCP server and opens the result.
- **Your Shortcut**: runs one of your own Shortcuts by name.
- The *AI Studio Neon* theme.

## Before you start

1. Put your Gemini API key into the Mac's keychain as `GEMINI_API_KEY`. The file never holds a key.
2. Install, then switch on only the permissions you want. What stays off is removed from your copy.

Nothing is sent until you press a key.

screenshots.caption: The AI Studio layout in its own Neon theme, with the guide and a chart under the keys
The how-to card and the week's images

permissions.reason: The Copy and Paste keys press ⌘C and ⌘V so a prompt can be copied and an answer pasted.
The My Shortcut key runs your own Shortcut named “AI Studio”.
The image, answer and video keys call Google's Gemini API and the Higgsfield MCP server.
The text on your clipboard is the prompt that is sent to those services.
A generated image is saved as a PNG in Downloads/iMacroPad and opened.
A generated video comes back as a web link, which is opened in your browser.

items.name: Sports scores
items.author: iMacroPad community
items.blurb: Your team on the pad: the next match, the last scores and the league table. Football, volleyball, basketball, NFL, NHL, F1 and more. Set your team or league on the widget (Edit ▸ the widget ▸ Live data); IDs are on thesportsdb.com (team page address). F1: your team’s and your driver’s standing and the next race in your time zone. Data: TheSportsDB free feed, ESPN and Jolpica (F1).
items.readme:
Your team on the pad: the next match, the last scores and the league table.

## What you get

- **F1**: your team's standing in the constructors' championship, your driver's standing, the next race with practice and qualifying in your own time zone, and the drivers' table.
- **Football, volleyball, NHL, NFL and more**: next match, last result, recent results and league tables.

## Set your team

1. Put a widget on a layout.
2. **Edit ▸ the widget ▸ Live data** and enter the team, driver or league.
3. F1 teams and drivers are written as Jolpica IDs: `ferrari`, `mclaren`, `red_bull`; `hamilton`, `leclerc`, `max_verstappen`.
4. Other team IDs are in the address of the team's page on thesportsdb.com.

Data comes from TheSportsDB's free feed, ESPN and Jolpica (F1). The Mac fetches it while the widget is on screen; the pad never calls these servers itself.

screenshots.caption: An F1 layout on an iPad mini: team, driver, next race and the drivers' table, live
Your team's standing: Ferrari, P2 in the constructors' championship
Your driver's standing: Lewis Hamilton, P3
The next race, practice and qualifying in your own time zone

permissions.reason: The Mac asks TheSportsDB, ESPN and Jolpica for fixtures, scores and tables. Only the team or league you set is sent.
The widgets show those answers and ask again every few minutes while on screen.
The scoreboard and the tables are small static HTML pages; no script, nothing loaded.

items.name: Status widgets
items.author: iMacroPad community
items.blurb: A general widget pack: a note card, a static HTML status board, a chart and two keys. Works on any layout.
items.readme:
A small, general widget pack to start from: a note card, a static HTML status board, a chart and two keys.

## What you get

- A Markdown note card.
- A status board drawn as static HTML (no script, nothing loaded).
- A bar chart.
- A **Screenshot** key and a **Scroll** dial.

Open any of them in Settings ▸ Widgets to see how it is made, then make a copy and change it. It works on any layout.

screenshots.caption: All five widgets on one layout, in the Nord theme
A Markdown note card and a static HTML status board
A line chart, the Screenshot key and the Scroll dial

permissions.reason: The status board is a small static HTML table; it has no script and loads nothing.
The Screenshot key presses its system shortcut and the Scroll dial scrolls the page.

items.name: Usage stats
items.author: iMacroPad community
items.blurb: Your own pad in numbers, on any layout or the screensaver: screen time today, the week as a chart, the layouts, Mac apps and themes you use most, and the keys you press most. Read from Settings ▸ Stats on this iPad; nothing leaves it.
items.readme:
Your own pad in numbers, on any layout or the screensaver.

## What you get

- **Today**: screen time and taps, with your top layouts.
- **This week**: screen time per day as a bar chart.
- **Leaderboard**: the layouts, Mac apps and themes you use most.
- **Top keys**: the keys you press most.

Everything is read from Settings ▸ Stats on this iPad. Nothing leaves it.
